mainKeyword: couch cushion support for sagging seats
metaTitle: Best Couch Cushion Supports for Sagging Seats
metaDescription: Six couch cushion supports compared on wood boards versus curved foam, thickness, foam density and fit, so you can fix a sagging sofa without buying a new one.
expertTake: The Meliusly 24 by 72 inch board is the top pick because 8 millimeter poplar plywood panels spread weight across the whole seat and have an anti-skid underside. The MLMTFI three-piece 45D curved foam set is the value pick when only the middle of a cushion sags. Skip a support if the springs or webbing underneath are broken, because a board hides the damage without fixing it.
introParagraphs: A sagging couch seat usually has one of two problems. Either the cushion foam has compressed, or the support beneath it has stretched or broken. A cushion support is a flat board or a curved foam pad that slides under the cushion and restores a level surface.

The product only works if it matches the cause and the fit. A board spreads load across the frame, a foam pad lifts a single dip, and neither helps if the cushion itself is worn out. Size, thickness and grip decide whether it stays put.

products.name: Meliusly 24 by 72 Inch Poplar Plywood Couch Support Board

specList.label: Fit
specList.value: Under the cushions on the frame

products.description:
Meliusly's board is 24 by 72 inches and built from 8 millimeter poplar LVL engineered wood panels, which the listing describes as moisture-controlled to stay flat. An anti-skid finish on the underside grips the sofa frame.

Long boards cover the whole seat base, so they support the load across several cushions instead of fighting one dip. Compared with the MLMTFI foam pads, the Meliusly is a structural fix and handles heavy sitters better, but it does nothing for a cushion whose foam has collapsed. It also raises the seat slightly, usually by a quarter to half an inch, which you will feel when you sit down.

Measure the frame opening before you buy, because the board must lie flat on the rails and not on the springs. Slide it in under the cushions, check that it sits level and sit on it for a day before deciding. If the sofa has a gap at the rear, trim nothing, and instead choose the closest size. Wood is stiff, so expect a firmer seat feel than the cushions had when new.
products.bestFor: Whole-seat sagging on a three-seat sofa with a flat frame.
pros: 8 mm poplar panels spread weight across the frame
24 by 72 inch size covers a full three-seat sofa
Anti-skid underside keeps the board in place
Moisture-controlled wood stays flat over time
cons: Does not restore a collapsed cushion
Raises the seat height and firmness slightly

products.name: LAVEVE Heavy Duty Solid Wood Couch Support Board, 21.5 by 70 Inch
products.description:
LAVEVE sells a multilayer solid wood board in 21.5 by 70 inches, wrapped in heavy-duty 600D Oxford fabric with silicone dots for grip. The listing says the board comes in 19 compatible sizes, from chairs to long sofas.

The size range is the main advantage, because the right fit matters more than the material. A board too wide for the frame buckles, and a board too narrow slides. Compared with the Meliusly, the LAVEVE adds a fabric wrap that keeps wood from scratching the cushion bottoms, while the Meliusly's panels fold for storage. The thickness is described as ergonomic and upgraded, so expect a stiff but unyielding layer.

Measure the width between the arms and the depth from the front rail to the back, then pick the nearest listed size. Fit the board under the cushions, tuck the Oxford cover edges flat and test it for a few evenings. Silicone dots grip the frame, but dust can reduce the grip, so wipe the board underneath now and then. A board suits a frame without sagging springs, where its job is to bridge the gaps.
products.bestFor: Sofas and loveseats where the right board size is the main challenge.
pros: 19 sizes let you match your seat closely
Multilayer solid wood resists bending
600D Oxford cover protects cushion bottoms
Silicone dots help grip the frame
cons: Stiff board changes the seat feel
Dust can reduce the silicone grip

products.name: MLMTFI 22 Inch Curved 45D Foam Couch Supports, 3 Pieces
products.description:
MLMTFI ships three 22 by 22 inch pads with an arch that reaches 2.4 inches at the center. The foam is rated 45D and described as high-resilience, and the arch is meant to fit the sagging area in the middle of the cushion.

Curved pads lift the dip without changing the whole seat height, so they are the gentler fix when only the middle sags. Against the Meliusly board, they cost less, install in seconds and leave the cushion free to flex, but they cannot bridge a broken frame. Three pieces means one per seat of a three-seat sofa, which is a sensible pack.

Measure the cushion before you buy, because the listing asks you to check that the 22 inch pad fits. Place each pad under the cushion with the arch facing up and the flat side down. If you feel the edge through the cushion, slide it further in or try a smaller pad. Foam compresses over time, so expect a slight loss of lift after a year.
products.bestFor: Three-seat sofas where each cushion sags in the middle.
pros: Arched shape lifts the sagging center
45D foam is high-resilience and recovers
Three pieces cover a three-seat sofa
Installs in seconds with no tools
cons: Foam compresses and loses lift over time
Cannot bridge a broken frame or springs

products.name: TFONSIGI 24 Inch 40D Foam Couch Support, 3-Piece Set
products.description:
TFONSIGI sells three 24 by 24 inch pads in 40D polyethylene foam, with other options at 20 by 20, 20 by 22 and 22 by 22 inches. The pads are 2 inches thick and gray.

A 24 inch pad covers deep seats better than 20 or 22 inch pads, so it suits large lounge sofas and sectionals. Compared with the MLMTFI at 22 inches with an arch, the TFONSIGI is flat and lifts the cushion evenly, which feels more like a new seat but does not target the center. Polyethylene foam is firm and resilient, and 40D is a mid-range density.

Place the pad under the cushion and square it to the frame so it does not poke out the front. If the cushion bottom has a zipper, check that the pad does not press the zipper pull into your leg. A flat pad suits cushions that sag across the whole seat, while an arched pad suits one that dips in the middle.
products.bestFor: Deep sofas and sectionals that need an even lift.
pros: 24 inch size suits deep seats and sectionals
Four size options reduce fit mistakes
40D foam is firm and resilient
Three pieces cover a three-seat sofa
cons: Flat shape does not target a center dip
Edge can show through thin cushions

products.name: Spongiduits 20 Inch Curved 40D Foam Couch Cushion Support
products.description:
Spongiduits makes a 20 by 20 by 2 inch curved pad in 40D high-density foam. The listing says you place it under a drooping cushion without tools or screws.

At 20 inches, this pad suits armchairs, loveseats and sofas with narrow seats, where bigger pads would hang out the front. Compared with the TFONSIGI at 24 inches, the Spongiduits is a closer fit for compact furniture, while the TFONSIGI better serves a lounge sofa. The curved shape helps lift a central sag, though the 2 inch thickness limits the fix to a mild dip.

Measure the cushion and subtract an inch for slack, because a pad as wide as the cushion will bunch at the edges. If the sag is deeper than an inch or two, a foam pad will only mask it. In that case, replace the cushion core with new foam and use the pad to even the base.
products.bestFor: Armchairs and loveseats with mild sagging.
pros: 20 inch size fits small seats
40D high-density foam resists compression
Curved shape lifts a mild dip
No tools or screws needed
cons: 2 inch thickness limits the lift for deep sags
Single pad covers only one seat

products.name: Sellmazon 24 Inch 35D Firm Trapezoid Foam Couch Support
products.description:
Sellmazon offers a 24 by 24 by 2 inch pad in 35D foam with a trapezoid profile that the listing calls firm. The pad sits under the cushion to make the seat firmer.

A trapezoid has sloped sides that reduce the ridge you can feel through a cushion, which suits a thin cushion. The 35D foam is slightly softer than the 40D and 45D alternatives, so it feels gentler but compresses sooner. Next to the TFONSIGI with 40D foam in the same size, the Sellmazon is the more comfortable pad and the shorter-lived one.

Place it with the wide side down and the narrow face up, and trim nothing. A foam support is best for mild sagging, such as a half inch to an inch, and for light to average sitters. For heavy use, step up to a board or a denser pad.
products.bestFor: Light sitters who want a gentle lift without a hard edge.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A board such as the Meliusly 24 by 72 or the LAVEVE 21.5 by 70 spreads load across the frame and fixes a seat that sags from worn webbing or springs. A foam pad such as the MLMTFI or TFONSIGI lifts a single cushion and costs less. Boards are stiff and raise the seat, while pads are softer. Choose a board for a frame problem and a pad for a cushion problem.

Measure the width of each seat opening and the depth from the front rail to the back. A pad that hangs over the edge will tilt, and one that is too small will shift. The MLMTFI is 22 inches, the Spongiduits 20 inches and the TFONSIGI 24 inches, and boards come in lengths such as 70 and 72 inches. Subtract about an inch for slack, and buy by measurement, not by sofa type.

Density in D shows how firm and durable foam is. The Sellmazon lists 35D, the Spongiduits and TFONSIGI 40D and the MLMTFI 45D. Higher numbers resist compression longer but feel firmer. Pick 40D or above for adult seats, and use lower density only for light users.

Most pads are about 2 inches thick, and the MLMTFI's arch reaches 2.4 inches at the center. Boards add roughly a quarter to half an inch. A seat that grows too tall puts your feet off the floor, so check the standard seat height of about 17 to 19 inches before adding more than an inch of support.

A support that slides is useless. The LAVEVE uses silicone dots on a 600D Oxford cover, and the Meliusly has an anti-skid finish. Foam pads rely on friction with the cushion, which holds better with fabric than with leather. If a pad creeps, add a strip of non-slip shelf liner underneath.

Lift the cushion and check the base. If the webbing is stretched or a spring has broken, a board bridges it, but a foam pad will not. If the cushion core is crushed, replace the foam. A support is a repair for mild to moderate sagging, not for a frame that has failed.

specDecoder.meaning: Density describes how much foam is in a cubic foot, and it predicts how long the pad keeps its lift. Higher density is firmer and lasts longer.
specDecoder.watchFor: The MLMTFI lists 45D, the Spongiduits and TFONSIGI list 40D and the Sellmazon lists 35D.

specDecoder.meaning: A curved pad is thicker at the center and tapers at the edges. It lifts the sagging middle without raising the edges.
specDecoder.watchFor: The MLMTFI arch reaches 2.4 inches, while the TFONSIGI is a flat 2 inches.

specDecoder.meaning: Board thickness is how much wood supports the load. Thicker or layered boards resist bending.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Meliusly uses 8 mm poplar panels, and the LAVEVE uses multilayer solid wood.

specDecoder.meaning: Anti-skid backing is a grippy finish that stops the support from sliding. It matters on smooth frames.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Meliusly and LAVEVE list grip features, while the foam pads rely on friction.

specDecoder.meaning: Pack count is how many supports you receive. It tells you how many seats you can fix.
specDecoder.watchFor: The MLMTFI and TFONSIGI include three pieces, but the Spongiduits and Sellmazon are single pads.

howWeEvaluated.title: Support method
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared boards with foam pads and weighed which problems each solves. The Meliusly and LAVEVE target frame sag, and the MLMTFI and TFONSIGI target cushion sag. The best product matches the cause.

howWeEvaluated.title: Materials and density
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at the Meliusly's 8 mm poplar, the LAVEVE's multilayer wood and the foam ratings from 35D to 45D. Higher density foam ranked higher for adult use. Listings without material detail scored lower.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit and size range
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared sizes from 20 inch pads to 72 inch boards. The LAVEVE's 19 sizes and the TFONSIGI's four options reduce fit errors. Fit decides whether the product works at all.

howWeEvaluated.title: Grip and stability
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at silicone dots, anti-skid finishes and foam friction. A support that slides fails quickly. Listings that explained grip scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Seat feel
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered how much each support raises and firms the seat. Boards are stiff, and the Sellmazon's softer 35D foam is gentle. A good fix restores level without a hard edge.

cards.label: Board
cards.text: The Meliusly and LAVEVE sit across the frame and fix sagging webbing or springs. They are firm and add a little seat height.

cards.label: Foam pad
cards.text: The MLMTFI, TFONSIGI, Spongiduits and Sellmazon lift individual cushions. They are softer and cheaper, but they cannot hold a broken frame.

howToChoose.note: Choose a board when the frame sags and a pad when only the cushion dips.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for wood boards, 40D or higher foam and a grip finish. Heavy sitters compress foam quickly and can crack thin boards.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The LAVEVE's multilayer board and the MLMTFI's 45D pads handle weight best.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: The whole seat sags or the sofa is heavily used, and a full board like the Meliusly will last for years.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Only one cushion sags, where a foam pad like the Spongiduits restores it quickly.

maintenance.why: Supports shift with use. Straightening them stops edges poking through the cushion.
Cushions compress where you sit. Rotating spreads wear so the support works with level foam.
A broken spring or loose webbing keeps sagging. Catching it early prevents damage to the cushion.
Foam supports lose lift gradually. Replace them when the seat starts to dip again.
Dust reduces grip on silicone dots and anti-skid surfaces. A damp cloth restores friction.

faq.q: Do couch cushion supports really work?
faq.a: They work for mild to moderate sagging when they match the cause. A board fixes a frame problem, and a foam pad lifts a cushion dip. Neither repairs a broken frame or a crushed cushion core.

faq.q: Board or foam: which lasts longer?
faq.a: A wood board usually lasts longer because it does not compress. Foam pads lose lift over a year or two, especially under heavy use.

faq.q: How do I measure for a support?
faq.a: Measure the width and depth of the seat opening on the frame, then subtract about an inch for slack. For boards, also measure the length across all seats.

faq.q: Will a support make the seat too hard?
faq.a: A board will feel firmer, and a thicker pad adds firmness too. If it is too hard, choose a softer foam like the Sellmazon's 35D.

faq.q: Can I use supports on a leather sofa?
faq.a: Yes, but leather cushions slide more, so choose a board with grip or add a non-slip liner. Keep the support away from the leather surface.

faq.q: When should I replace the cushions instead?
faq.a: If the foam core is crushed or the cushion has lost most of its thickness, a support only masks the problem. Replace the foam, then add a support if needed.
